Dear Secretary Reese:

Northbrook Lyons Falls, LLC (NBLF or Licensee), managed and operated by KEI (USA) Power
Management, Inc., filed a Final License Application (FLA) for the Lyons Falls Hydroelectric Project
(FERC No. 2548) (Project) with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC or
Commission) on May 31, 2024. On August 29, 2024, Commission staff requested that NBLF
provide additional information for the FLA. NBLF filed responses to FERC’s letter on November
27, 2024, February 11, 2025, March 27, 2025, and May 28, 2025.

On June 10, 2026, FERC requested additional information related to the FLA. On October 2,
2026, FERC granted an extension of time until October 22, 2026, to respond to the information
requests. NBLF herein provides responses to the additional information requests.

General

1.       Section 16.10(a)(10) of the Commission’s regulations requires that any applicant
proposing to expand the project to encompass additional lands, include in its application a
statement that the applicant has notified, by certified mail, property owners on the additional
lands to be encompassed by the project and governmental agencies and subdivisions likely to
be interested in or affected by the proposed expansion. Commission staff’s August 29, 2024
letter, included deficiency item 2 of Schedule A, requesting that Northbrook file a statement of
compliance with section 16.10(a)(1) of the Commission’s regulations for land that it is proposing
to include in the project boundary that is not included in the project boundary under the current
license. Northbrook’s March 27, 2025 response states that the proposed modifications to the
Lyons Falls Development are anticipated to be within the footprint of the existing primary
powerhouse and, therefore, notification of abutters is not required.

         The Exhibit G maps filed on February 11, 2025, as part of the relicense application,
indicate that Northbrook’s proposed project boundary for relicensing includes land that is not in
the most recent Exhibit G project boundary maps approved on March 24, 1993. 1 For example,
the proposed project boundary shown on the Exhibit G maps filed with the relicense application
includes land adjacent to the transmission lines of the Gouldtown and Lyons Falls
Developments, land adjacent to the Lyons Falls Development powerhouse, and land adjacent to
the impoundments of the Kosterville and Gouldtown Developments that is not included in the
project boundary shown on the Exhibit G maps approved in 1993. Please file a statement that
Northbrook has notified, by certified mail, property owners on the additional lands in the
proposed project boundary, and governmental agencies and subdivisions likely to be interested
in or affected by the proposed expansion.

Response

On September 2, 2026, NBLF notified, by certified mail, property owners on the additional lands
in the proposed Project boundary, and governmental agencies and subdivisions likely to be
interested in or affected by the proposed expansion. Proof of certified mailing is included as
Attachment 1.

estimate of the dependable capacity and average annual energy production in kilowatt-hours for

annual energy production of the project in kilowatt-hours, including separate values for the
Lyons Falls, Gouldtown, and Kosterville Developments, based on the operation proposed in the
license application.

Exhibit F

4.      Section 4.41(g)(1) of the Commission’s regulations requires that an application include
an Exhibit F that contains drawings showing all major project structures in sufficient detail to
provide a full understanding of the project, including plans (overhead view), elevations (front
view), profiles (side view), and sections. The Exhibit F drawings filed on March 27, 2025, do not
show: (1) a section drawing of the Gouldtown Development south dam that includes the sluice
gate and low-level outlet gate; (2) a section drawing of the Gouldtown Development’s earthen
fuse plug embankment; (3) a front view of the Lyons Falls Development dam; (4) a section

include this information. Please file all Exhibit F information as Critical Energy Infrastructure
Information pursuant to section 388.113 of the Commission’s regulations.

Response

The SDR filed on March 27, 2025, does not include a section view and stability analysis of the
Gouldtown Development’s earthen fuse plug embankment. Please revise the SDR to include
this information.

1.     In an order issued on March 30, 2016 (2016 Order), 1 Commission staff authorized
Northbrook’s proposal to amend the current license by increasing the authorized installed
capacity of the Lyons Falls Development from 5.59 to 11.2 megawatts (MW) through:

(1) demolishing the existing primary powerhouse and mothballing the secondary powerhouse;
and (2) constructing a new powerhouse that includes two turbine-generator units that each have
an installed capacity of 5.6 MW and a hydraulic capacity of 1,342 cfs. Northbrook has not
started construction of the authorized modifications to the Lyons Falls Development. 2 The
revised Exhibit A of the relicense application, filed on March 27, 2025, states that Northbrook is
proposing to modify the Lyons Falls Development by replacing the existing powerhouse and
associated infrastructure with facilities that would have an installed capacity of 7.5 MW,
including three turbine-generator units that each have an installed capacity of 2.5 MW and a
hydraulic capacity of 500 cfs. Please provide the following information that is necessary for
Commission staff’s review of project facilities and potential environmental effects of the
proposed modifications:

   (a)      confirmation that Northbrook proposes to construct the facilities described in the

            the 2016 Order; 3 and

            modifications authorized in the 2016 Order, including but not limited to:

            2. Exhibit B to include a statement of project operation and resource utilization,

               modifications to the Lyons Falls Development;

that it owns the substation and transformer that serve as the interconnection point with the
electric grid for the Lyons Falls Development. Please revise Exhibit A to explain whether there
are any non-project uses (e.g., the interconnection of any non-project facilities) for the
substation and transformer. This information is necessary for staff to distinguish between
project and non-project facilities.

Gouldtown Development’s interconnection point with the electric grid. This information is
necessary for staff to distinguish between project and non-project facilities.

There are no non-project uses for the substation and transformer that serve as the Gouldtown
Development’s interconnection point with the electric grid.

4.     Please clarify whether the project draws station service power from the electric grid
when the turbine-generator units are offline and, if so, identify the transmission facilities and
interconnections that are used to supply power to each of the project’s developments. This
information is necessary for staff to distinguish between project and non-project facilities.

All three developments draw power from electric grid when turbines are offline for lights, fans,

Northbrook Lyons Falls, LLC (NBLF), managed and operated by KEI (USA) Power Management,

BACKGROUND
On May 6, 1986, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC or Commission) issued a
new license for the Project. 1 The Lyons Falls Hydroelectric Project consists of three
developments: Lyons Falls, Gouldtown, and Kosterville. On March 24, 1993, the Commission
issued an order amending the Project license to establish a total authorized installed generating
capacity of 8,640 kilowatts (kW). Each development’s authorized installed capacity is as follows:
Lyons Falls Mill Development with 5,590 kW, Gouldtown Development with 2,000 kW, and
Kosterville Development with 1,050 kW. 2

On March 30, 2016 3, FERC issued an Order Amending License and Revising Annual Charges.
The amendment increased both the installed generating capacity and hydraulic capacity at the
Lyons Falls Development. The modifications included the following components:

    •   Demolition and Decommissioning: Demolition of the existing four-unit primary
        powerhouse and mothballing of the secondary single-unit powerhouse.
    •   Intake and Trashrack Structure: Construction of a new combined intake and trashrack
        structure measuring approximately 60 feet in length, 45 feet in width, and 40 feet in
        height, to be located adjacent to the left abutment of the dam.
    •   Penstocks: Installation of two steel penstocks, approximately 11.5 feet in diameter and
        75 feet in length.
    •   New Powerhouse: Construction of a new concrete and masonry powerhouse along the
        left bank of the river, largely within the footprint of the existing primary powerhouse to be
        demolished. The new powerhouse would house two generating units.

Implementation of these modifications would increase the installed capacity of the Lyons Falls
Mill Development from 5,590 kilowatts (kW) to 11,200 kW and increase its hydraulic capacity from
1,170 cubic feet per second (cfs) to 2,684 cfs. As a result, the total installed capacity of the Lyons
Falls Project would increase to 14,250 kW.

The Project is currently undergoing relicensing. NBLF filed a Final License Application (FLA) on
May 31, 2024 4. FERC requested additional information on August 29, 2024 5. NBLF responded to
this request on November 27, 2024 6, February 11, 2025 7, March 27, 2025 8, and May 28, 2025 9.
In the March 17, 2026, filing, NBLF stated it had revised the configuration of the redevelopment
to a design that differed from the 2016 Order. The new design would include installation of three
horizontal Francis turbine-generator units, each rated at 2,500 kW, for a total installed capacity of
7,500 kW. Additionally, NBLF stated the new design would include demolition of both
powerhouses. Herein, the 7,500 kW design is referred to as the Redevelopment Project.

FERC issued a second additional information request on June 10, 2026 10. NBLF has not filed a
response to FERC’s June 10, 2026, letter at the time of this letter.

referred to as historic properties. The statute also requires that the Advisory Council on Historic

Compliance with Section 106 typically involves consultation with the appropriate State Historic
Preservation Officer (SHPO) to evaluate potential effects on historic properties and to identify
measures to avoid, minimize, or mitigate adverse impacts. Relicensing of the Project constitutes
a federal undertaking subject to Section 106 of the NHPA (54 U.S.C. § 306101).

As part of the relicensing effort and in a letter dated June 2, 2015 13, the Commission designated
the licensee as its non-federal representative for the purpose of conducting Section 106
consultation with the New York SHPO and Tribal Nations. Pursuant to Article 409 of the Project
license, NBLF consulted with the New York SHPO and Oneida Indian Nation. The Oneida Indian
Nation, in correspondence dated April 29, 2015, indicated that the relicensing of the facilities
would not adversely affect historic properties of religious or cultural significance to the Nation. The
New York SHPO stated in a letter dated May 8, 2015, that the proposed relicensing would have
no effect on historic properties.

On November 21, 2025, the New York SHPO completed the review of the Final License
Application (FLA) and requested an Architectural Resources Survey and provided the following

        We note that the Lyons Falls Mill Development is eligible for listing in the State and

                redevelopment project is to be separately submitted to our office for review.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The existing Project includes an L-shaped concrete dam, a concrete flood gate structure with four
steel gates, a flow intake rack structure, and a headworks structure leading to three exposed steel
penstocks. The facility also contains two historic powerhouses: a concrete structure with a brick
superstructure housing a single vertical turbine-generator unit (No. 1 powerhouse) built in 1922,
and a second concrete structure with a brick superstructure containing four horizontal turbine-
generator units (No. 2 powerhouse) built in 1896. Also present is an adjacent former paper mill
building of brick construction that contains electrical equipment and remnants of historic industrial

operations. Additional features include an open-air transformer on a concrete slab and associated
aerial electrical lines connecting to a nearby substation. Collectively, these components reflect
the site’s historic industrial use and hydroelectric development.

The Redevelopment Project, to be further detailed in NBLF’s revised FLA to be filed on or by
September 22, 2026 in response to FERC’s June 10, 2026, letter, would not involve modification
of the dam or flood gate structures, which would remain in place. However, the undertaking would
result in the removal of several contributing or potentially contributing elements of the historic
industrial complex. Specifically, the redevelopment includes removal of all existing turbine-
generator units (five total), associated electrical control and power equipment, both existing
powerhouses, all exposed steel penstock systems and their concrete supports, existing walkways
and platforms, and the remnants of the former brick mill building. These actions would alter the
existing configuration, material integrity, and historic character of the industrial complex.

The Redevelopment Project would include construction of a new powerhouse consisting of a
concrete foundation with a steel superstructure to be located in the same general footprint as the
existing No. 2 powerhouse and extending onto a small adjacent parcel acquired to accommodate
the dimensions of the new powerhouse.. The new powerhouse would contain three horizontal
Francis-style turbine-generator units, each rated at 2.5 megawatts. While the general location of
power generation infrastructure would remain consistent with historic use, the replacement of
multiple historic structures with a single modern facility would represent a substantial change in
design, materials, and workmanship.

River flows would continue to pass through the existing intake rack structure and a modified
headworks and would be conveyed to the new powerhouse via three exposed steel penstocks:
one penstock connected directly to a turbine-generator unit and a second penstock that bifurcates
into two branches, each supplying a separate turbine-generator unitDischarge from the new
powerhouse would occur in approximately the same location as the existing No. 2 powerhouse
outfall. Electrical systems would be consolidated within the new powerhouse, and modifications
to the transformer area would include installation of a new transformer with spill containment and
new aerial electrical lines.

Construction activities would include selective removal of exposed bedrock to accommodate
installation of new civil features, as well as temporary dewatering measures such as cofferdams
adjacent to the existing No. 2 powerhouse outfall. While these activities would be temporary in
nature, they would occur within the historic property area and may introduce short-term
disturbances to contributing features and their setting.

Overall, the undertaking would retain certain primary structural elements (e.g., dam and flood gate
structures) but would remove and replace multiple buildings and features that contribute to the
historic industrial character of the site (see Attachment 2). As such, the Project has the potential
to affect the integrity of the property, including aspects of design, materials, workmanship, and
setting, and warrants further evaluation under Section 106 of the NHPA.

The Lyons Falls Hydroelectric Complex (USN 04946.000071) is eligible for listing in the NRHP
under Criterion A for its local significance in the areas of commerce, industry, and engineering.
The site has a period of significance that spans from the 1890s to the 1970s. Contributing features
to the site include, the 1923 powerhouse, 1896/1923/ca.1940 penstock, 1922 concrete gravity
dam, 1940 intake structure, 1974 penstock, and remnants of the 1896 powerhouse.

The Parker Truss Bridge over Moose River (National Bridge Inventory [NBI] 3339760, USN
04910.000024) is a 1942 steel bridge on Shibley Road between Goulds Mill and Kosterville. The
bridge abutments are constructed of cut stone and concrete, and the roadbed surface consists of
metal grating. The bridge is eligible for listing in the NRHP at the state level of significance under
Criterion C in the area of engineering. This property is located 1.9 km (1.2 mi) ESE of the
Redevelopment Project.

The Black River Canal (USN 04312.000015) in the Booneville vicinity has been determined
eligible for listing in the NRHP as a contributing element of the New York Canal System (New

the area of engineering. Although USN 04312.000015 indicates much of the original canal north

Redevelopment Project area. The site was recorded in 1984, and its status is currently
‘Undetermined’ for inclusion on the NRHP.

NYSM Site 7112 is described as ‘Traces of Occupation’ and encompasses a broad swath of the
Black River from the Onieda – Lewis County border north to the confluence of the Moose River
and Black Rivers. The site area was described in 1922, and its status is currently ‘Undetermined’
for inclusion on the NRHP.

The Gydesem Farm Site (NYSM Site 9114) is a broad area of occupation centered on the
Gydesem Farm originally located at the confluence of the Moose and Black Rivers which includes
the Lyons Falls Redevelopment Project area. The site area was recorded in 1968, and its status
is currently ‘Undetermined’ for inclusion on the NRHP.

SUMMARY AND CONCLUSION
Pursuant to Article 409 of the License, and as requested in the November 21, 2025 letter from
the NY SHPO, NBLF hereby submits the initial consultation notification for the Proposed
Redevelopment of the Lyon Falls Hydroelectric Project.

The Redevelopment Project will require the necessary environmental permits and approvals from
the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (NYSDEC), FERC, and the U.S.
Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS), as applicable.
At the time of this notification, the Project constitutes a federal undertaking subject to Section 106
of the NHPA (54 U.S.C. § 306101) and its implementing regulations at 36 CFR Part 800.
Consistent with the Final License Application, FERC will serve as the lead federal agency
responsible for coordinating the federal review process.

Construction activities are anticipated to begin in April 2027 and are expected to be completed
within approximately eight (8) months.

B.1.1          Operation during Normal Flow

B.1.1.1        Lyons Falls Mill Development Operations

Existing Lyons Falls Mill Development

The Lyons Falls Mill Development operates in a run-of-river (ROR) mode and operations are
semi-automatic. The three flood control gates at the Lyons Falls Mill Development are rack-and-
pinion operated. The intake gates for each of the three penstocks are electrically actuated gates.
The Lyons Falls Mill Development attempts to generate for the entire year; however, seasonal
interruptions periodically occur due to frazil ice accumulations on the trashracks and in the
penstocks.

Spillway elevation is generally maintained at 806.5 feet as a result of maintaining the 26-inch-high
flashboards on top of the spillway crest, which has an elevation of 804.3 feet National Geodetic
Vertical Datum of 1929 (NGVD29). All river flows between 80 cubic feet per second (cfs)
(minimum operating point for Unit 9) and 1,170 cfs (maximum hydraulic capacity of all 5
generating units) are passed through the units.

Proposed Redevelopment of Lyons Falls Mill Development

As part of the redevelopment project, no changes are planned for the three flood control gates.
However, one of the three existing intake gates will be removed as it will no longer be required.
The remaining two gates will be retained, and opportunities to enhance their operation, including
potential automation, will be evaluated during the detailed design phase. The facility will continue
to operate in a run-of-river mode and generating year-round, although seasonal interruptions may
still occur due to frazil ice accumulations on the trashracks and in the penstocks. Spillway
elevation is generally maintained at 806.5 feet as a result of maintaining the 26-inch-high
flashboards on top of the spillway crest, which has an elevation of 804.3 feet NGVD29. All river

B.1.1.2         Gouldtown Development Operations

The Gouldtown Development operates in a ROR mode and operations are semi-automatic. The

generally maintained at 852.0 feet as a result of maintaining the 3.0-foot-high flashboards on top
of the spillway crest. The Project’s turbine utilizes available streamflow up to the hydraulic

In accordance with Article 404, NBLF discharges a continuous minimum flow of 5 cfs (or inflow,

of fish, recreation, and aesthetic resources in the north channel between the dam and the
confluence with the south channel. The required 5 cfs is provided through a bypass flow pipe
located below the level of the flashboards that is always open.

B.1.1.3         Kosterville Development Operations

The Kosterville Development operates in a ROR mode and operations are manual. Each of the
two compartments of the flume have manually operated, rack-and-pinion intake gates. The
spillway elevation is generally maintained at 889.5 feet. The Project’s turbines utilize streamflow
up to the hydraulic capacity of 540 cfs.

Existing Lyons Falls Mill Development

cfs, Lyons Falls Mill is operated at full gate (full hydraulic capacity of the five turbines). Flows in
excess of the hydraulic capacity are passed over the Development’s spillway or through the
Development’s sluice gate. As necessary, the flood gates are utilized to accommodate passage
of higher flows.

Proposed Redevelopment of Lyons Falls Mill Development

During periods of high flow, when inflow equals or exceeds the plant’s hydraulic capacity of 1,500
cfs, Lyons Falls Mill is operated at full gate (full hydraulic capacity of the turbines). Flows in excess

B.1.1          Operation during Normal Flow

B.1.1.1        Lyons Falls Mill Development Operations

Existing Lyons Falls Mill Development

The Lyons Falls Mill Development operates in a run-of-river (ROR) mode and operations are
semi-automatic. The three flood control gates at the Lyons Falls Mill Development are rack-and-
pinion operated. The intake gates for each of the three penstocks are manually operated
electrically actuatedby rack-and-pinion gates. The Lyons Falls Mill Development attempts to
generate for the entire year; however, seasonal interruptions periodically occur due to frazil ice
accumulations on the trashracks and in the penstocks.

Spillway elevation is generally maintained at 806.5 feet as a result of maintaining the 26-inch-high
flashboards on top of the spillway crest, which has an elevation of 804.3 feet National Geodetic
Vertical Datum of 1929 (NGVD29). All river flows between 80 cubic feet per second (cfs)
(minimum operating point for Unit 9) and 1,170 cfs (maximum hydraulic capacity of all 5
generating units) are passed through the units.

Proposed Redevelopment of Lyons Falls Mill Development

The Lyons Falls Mill Development operates in a ROR mode and operations are semi-automatic.
The three flood control gates at the Lyons Falls Mill Development are manually operated. The
Lyons Falls Mill Development will attempt to generate for the entire year; however, seasonal
interruptions periodically occur due to frazil ice accumulations on the trashracks and in the
penstocks.As part of the redevelopment project, no changes are planned for the three flood
control gates. However, one of the three existing intake gates will be removed as it will no longer
be required. The remaining two gates will be retained, and opportunities to enhance their
operation, including potential automation, will be evaluated during the detailed design phase. The

B.1.1.2        Gouldtown Development Operations

The Gouldtown Development operates in a ROR mode and operations are semi-automatic. The
trash rake at the intake is manually operated and electrically powered. The spillway elevation is
generally maintained at 852.0 feet as a result of maintaining the 3.0-foot-high flashboards on top
of the spillway crest. The Project’s turbine utilizes available streamflow up to the hydraulic
capacity of 726 cfs.

In accordance with Article 404, NBLF discharges a continuous minimum flow of 5 cfs (or inflow,
whichever is less) from the north channel dam at the Gouldtown Development for the protection
of fish, recreation, and aesthetic resources in the north channel between the dam and the
confluence with the south channel. The required 5 cfs is provided through a bypass flow pipe
located below the level of the flashboards that is always open.

B.1.1.3        Kosterville Development Operations

The Kosterville Development operates in a ROR mode and operations are manual. Each of the
two compartments of the flume have manually operated, rack-and-pinion intake gates. The
spillway elevation is generally maintained at 889.5 feet. The Project’s turbines utilize streamflow
up to the hydraulic capacity of 540 cfs.

B.1.2.1        Lyons Falls Mill Development

Existing Lyons Falls Mill Development

During periods of high flow, when inflow equals or exceeds the plant’s hydraulic capacity of 1,170
cfs, Lyons Falls Mill is operated at full gate (full hydraulic capacity of the five turbines). Flows in
excess of the hydraulic capacity are passed over the Development’s spillway or through the

of higher flows.

Proposed Redevelopment of Lyons Falls Mill Development

During periods of high flow, when inflow equals or exceeds the plant’s hydraulic capacity of 1,500
cfs, Lyons Falls Mill is operated at full gate (full hydraulic capacity of the turbines). Flows in excess
of the hydraulic capacity are passed over the Development’s spillway or through the
Development’s sluice gate. As necessary, the flood gates are utilized to accommodate passage
of higher flows.

B.1.2.2         Gouldtown Development

Flows in excess of the Gouldtown Development’s hydraulic capacity of 726 cfs are passed over
the spillway. The Gouldtown Development utilizes an engineered fuse plug that is designed to
release under high river flow conditions. This feature helps prevent upstream flooding and
embankment failure during high-flow events within the watershed.

B.1.2.3         Kosterville Development

Flows in excess of the Kosterville Development’s hydraulic capacity of 540 cfs are passed over
the spillway.

generation), NBLF ceases operations of the Project’s turbines, and all flow is passed over the
flashboards or spillway.

B.2.1.1           Lyons Falls Mill Development

To determine the flows at Lyons Falls Mill, the flows at the Black River and Moose River gages
were prorated by a factor of approximately 1.4 and 1.2, respectively. The Black River factor of 1.4
was determined as the drainage area of the Black River at Lyons Falls Mill (433 square miles)
divided by the drainage area of the Black River gage (304 square miles). The Moose River factor
of 1.2 was determined as the drainage area of the Moose River at Lyons Falls Mill (433 square
miles) divided by the drainage area of the Moose River gage (363 square miles). The prorated
flows were then added to determine the total contributing flow at Lyons Falls Mill. For periods
where the Moose River data was not available, the flows at the Black River gage were prorated
by a factor of approximately 2.8. This factor was determined by dividing the total drainage area at
the Lyons Falls Mill (866 square miles) by the drainage area at the Black River gage (304 square
miles).

$5,000 per installed kilowatt (kW). Based on this evaluation, the estimated fair market value of

license from earnings in excess of a fair return on such investment): (a) unappropriated surplus;
(b) aggregate credit balances of current depreciated accounts; and (c) aggregate appropriations
of surplus or income held in amortization, sinking fund, or similar reserves.
